details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> vulkan: cap scalar flash attention at 8 rows for large heads on Qualcomm (#30829) With head sizes above 128 and KV >= 1024, scalar flash attention uses 16 rows per workgroup. On the Qualcomm Adreno driver this variant spills registers to scratch memory (264 bytes per invocation on the X1-85, none at 8 rows) and runs about 40x slower. The largest test-backend-ops case then becomes a single dispatch of several seconds, past the Windows GPU timeout, and the test never completes on the X1 Elite. Use at most 8 rows per workgroup on Qualcomm when hsk or hsv > 128. Smaller heads keep 16 rows, which is faster for them on the X2 Elite. Adreno X1-85, FLASH_ATTN_EXT hsk=256 kv=4096: nb=64 711 ms -> 17 ms, nb=512 no result -> 125 ms; test-backend-ops completes. Adreno X2-90: Gemma 4 E4B pp512 at depth 4096 with flash attention 81-90 -> 117 t/s. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/65813913> **macOS/iOS:

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> ggml-rpc : fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes (#30415) * ggml-rpc: fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed handshakes rpc_dispatcher::start() aborted the whole process (GGML_ABORT -> SIGABRT) when the endpoint could not be parsed, the transport failed to initialise, the socket could not connect, or the HELLO handshake failed. A typo in --rpc or a temporarily down node killed the host application, and the reason went to a log stream the host may never see. Make the connect-time failure reportable instead of fatal: start() returns bool (LOG_ERROR + false; the dispatcher thread only starts after a successful handshake), negotiate_hello() returns false on a half-open socket, get_dispatcher() returns nullptr and does not cache failed attempts, and every consumer treats nullptr as "endpoint did not answer" with the conservative behaviour of its domain (allocation -> nullptr, alloc-size -> lower bound, device memory -> 0/0, events -> no-o

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> vulkan: add tiled-transpose concat shader for Qwen models (#30591) * vulkan: tiled transpose for dim-0 concat with a transposed source The delta-net conv-state path does ggml_transpose() straight into a dim-0 ggml_concat(), so the generic concat kernel reads src1 with the transposed stride, one element per thread, and neighbouring lanes land on different cache lines. Stage a 32x32 tile through shared memory instead, which keeps both the load and the store coalesced. 33 columns pads away the bank conflicts. Gated narrowly: dim 0, 2D, unquantized 4-byte elements, contiguous src0/dst rows, and src1 actually transposed. Everything else falls through to the existing kernel. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on gfx1151/RADV, 30 gated-delta-net layers: the CONCAT op goes 11877 us -> 957 us, and pp2048 at ub2048 goes 1224 -> 1628 t/s. Generated text is unchanged. The approach follows the tiled transposed concat Gaetan Puleo wrote for the HIP backend in his Strix Halo fork. Co-Authored-By: Claude

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> CUDA: move graph and concurrent stream state out of common.cuh (#32001) ggml_cuda_graph, ggml_cuda_concurrent_event and ggml_cuda_stream_context are only used by ggml-cuda.cu, but keeping them in common.cuh meant any change to them rebuilt every CUDA translation unit.
